title: Scaling stateful Gemini 4 Argon agent sessions on GKE: Connection draining, startup boost, and session persistence
why_read: A fairly concrete Kubernetes/GKE operations writeup on handling long-running, stateful AI agent sessions, useful to platform engineers deploying such workloads.
analysis: This article addresses real infrastructure pain points of running long-lived, stateful streaming AI agent sessions on Kubernetes, including CPU throttling at startup, connection draining during scale-down, and session state persistence. It specifically discusses using GKE features like VPA CPU startup boost and GCPBackendPolicy connection draining to handle these failure modes. This is a practically-focused ops piece relevant to teams running multi-turn LLM agents in production rather than simple stateless request/response services. The reference to a 'Gemini 4 Argon' product name is unusual and should be treated skeptically as it may not correspond to an actual publicly documented model.
